pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.3.3)
- B8.3.3.1 — Perform a single transformation (i.e. rotation) on a 2D shape using graph paper (including technology) and describe the properties of the image under the transformation (i.e. congruence).

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- identify rotations in everyday life and describe them as clockwise or anticlockwise
- rotate points and shapes about the origin through 90°, 180° and 270°
- state the coordinate rules for rotation
- determine the angle and direction of a rotation from an object and its image
- verify that rotation produces congruent shapes

pages.title: Rotation in everyday life
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Understand rotation and identify real-life situations involving rotation.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.3.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Rotation** — A **rotation** turns a shape about a fixed point called the **centre of rotation** through a given **angle** in a given **direction** (clockwise or anticlockwise). Every point stays the same distance from the centre.
Examples of rotation in daily life: the hands of a clock (clockwise), a ceiling fan, a wheel of a bicycle or a corn mill, a door turning on its hinges, the blades of a windmill, a spinning top, and the Earth turning on its axis (anticlockwise when viewed from above the North Pole).
[[fig:m8-f45|Figure 12.1: Clockwise and anticlockwise turns]]

pages.title: Rotating shapes on the coordinate plane
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Draw rotation images in a coordinate plane and determine the angle of rotation.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.3.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Rules for rotation about the origin** — **90° anticlockwise** (= 270° clockwise): (x, y) → (−y, x). **180°** (either direction): (x, y) → (−x, −y). **90° clockwise** (= 270° anticlockwise): (x, y) → (y, −x).
[[fig:m8-f46|Figure 12.2: The point P(4, 2) rotated about the origin]]
## ✏️ Example 12.1
Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1) and C(4, 3). Rotate it about the origin through a) 90° anticlockwise b) 180° c) 90° clockwise. State the coordinates of each image.
**Solution**
| **Object** | **90° anticlockwise (−y, x)** | **180° (−x, −y)** | **90° clockwise (y, −x)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| A(1, 1) | A′(−1, 1) | A″(−1, −1) | A‴(1, −1) |
| B(4, 1) | B′(−1, 4) | B″(−4, −1) | B‴(1, −4) |
| C(4, 3) | C′(−3, 4) | C″(−4, −3) | C‴(3, −4) |
[[fig:m8-f47]]
Figure 12.3: Triangle ABC and its three images
## ✏️ Example 12.2
Find the angle and direction of the rotation about the origin that maps P(3, 1) onto P′(−1, 3).
**Solution**
Compare with the rules: (3, 1) → (−1, 3) is (x, y) → (−y, x), which is a **rotation of 90° anticlockwise** about the origin. You can check with a protractor: the angle ∠POP′ is 90°, measured anticlockwise.
## ✏️ Example 12.3
Determine the angle of rotation by construction when the centre is not given.
**Solution**
Join one object point to its image (e.g. A to A′) and construct the perpendicular bisector of AA′. Do the same for B and B′. The two bisectors meet at the **centre of rotation** O. Measure ∠AOA′ with a protractor: this is the angle of rotation.

pages.title: Rotation and congruence
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Investigate the concept of congruent shapes.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.3.1.3
Measure the sides and angles of triangle ABC and of each of its images in Example 12.1. You will find:
| **Property** | **Object ABC** | **Images under rotation** |
|---|---|---|
| Side lengths | AB = 3, BC = 2, AC = √13 | the same |
| Angles | 90° at B, others equal | the same |
| Area | 3 square units | the same |
| Orientation (order of labels A → B → C) | anticlockwise | still anticlockwise |
> 🔑 **Key idea: Rotation preserves size and shape** — The image of a shape under a rotation is **congruent** to the object: all lengths, angles and areas are unchanged, and (unlike a reflection) the shape is **not** turned over.

pages.title: Exercise 12.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 12.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Draw triangle (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 4). Rotate it 180° about the origin. Show by measuring that the image is congruent to the object.
2. Which transformations studied so far always produce congruent images? (reflection, translation, rotation)

questions.q: Draw triangle (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 4). Rotate it 180° about the origin. Show by measuring that the image is congruent to the object.
Which transformations studied so far always produce congruent images? (reflection, translation, rotation)

parts.a: All three: reflection, translation and rotation

pages.title: Chapter 12 summary
pages.body:
- A rotation is described by its centre, angle and direction.
- About the origin: 90° anticlockwise (x, y) → (−y, x); 180° (x, y) → (−x, −y); 90° clockwise (x, y) → (y, −x).
- The centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of every object–image pair.
- Rotations produce congruent images with the same orientation.
